summary.headline: Persistent Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to USD 487.6M, but EBIT margin fell to 15% and reported PAT dropped 25.4% on Nagarro deal costs.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 7.8% QoQ and 20% YoY in USD to USD 487.6M, the 26th sequential quarter of growth, with rupee revenue of Rs 46,639M (+30.3% YoY). EBIT margin was 15% (down 100 bps QoQ and 130 bps YoY) as wage hikes and a 90 bps amortisation hit from the large software deal offset ESOP and currency tailwinds. Reported PAT of Rs 3,515.1M (7.5% margin) was hit by about 3.1% from Nagarro transaction costs, while operating PAT rose 5% YoY to Rs 4,951.5M. Bookings slowed: TCV was USD 633.5M and ACV USD 481M, with management citing deal slippage and a decision-making slowdown linked to Middle East dynamics. The Nagarro acquisition is progressing, with about 94% of shares tendered and closing guided to Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.5% YoY in USD terms.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 8.5% YoY, attributed to one acquired key client ramping down and one fixed-price engagement completing its planned ramp-down; management called these client-specific.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.4% YoY; rest of world grew 67% YoY on a smaller base.

segments.name: Software, High-Tech and Emerging
segments.commentary: Grew 28.5% YoY, driven by the large software deal from last quarter and the new Software Reinvention offering.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 16.2% YoY, supported by a vendor consolidation win at a large financial services client.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 12% YoY; management said growth should resume, citing a slowdown from a couple of customer-specific dynamics.

guidance_outlook: EBIT margin aspiration of 16-17%; management said it is an aspiration, not guidance, with no year-end target committed.
Nagarro deal closing expected by Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27; remaining RBI, Austria and Spain FDI approvals expected within 4-8 weeks.
Nagarro acquisition one-time expenses of about USD 50M in total over 3-4 quarters; about USD 19-20M incurred in Q2 and USD 25-30M more to come.
Post-closing, intent to squeeze out minority shareholders (about 94% acquired) and an estimated 5-6 months to integrate the two companies.
Acquisition debt cost assumed at 5-6% net; USD 1.25B debt and equity raise planned to replace the Euro 1.4B bridge loan, including USD 450M equity or equity-linked instruments.
Transaction-related one-time costs may be treated as an exception for ESOP vesting conditions (12% revenue growth and 12% EPS growth), subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose by 958 QoQ to 29,598 at end of Q2 FY27.
Utilisation fell 70 bps QoQ to 85.8%, reflecting proactive hiring for large-deal ramp-up; utilisation drag was about 20 bps on EBIT margin.
Trailing 12-month attrition was 11.9%, down from 12.3% in Q1.

The large software deal (about USD 650M over 6.5 years) carries about USD 4M per quarter of added amortisation on third-party licences and cloud spend, a 90 bps EBIT margin hit that management expects to ease as spend is optimised and revenue scales.
Internal AI IP (SASVA, iAURA, Gen AI) development cost includes significant people cost plus tools; management said it can rise QoQ with new feature development.
demand_pricing: Q2 bookings were USD 633.5M TCV and USD 481M ACV, versus Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M which included the USD 650M large deal; management said some deals slipped and decision-making slowed in recent weeks, linked to Middle East dynamics.
Top 5 customers grew 38.9% YoY, top 10 grew 29.9%, top 20 grew 25%, top 50 grew 24%, top 100 grew 21.6%.
Customers above USD 20M annual revenue rose from 12 to 13, above USD 10M from 25 to 34, above USD 5M from 56 to 60, and above USD 1M from 191 to 280.
BFSI demand themes: vendor consolidation, data modernisation for AI and legacy (mainframe) modernisation; management did not give formal guidance but said all segments should grow well.

Software Reinvention Services targets AI-native product development and cost reduction of legacy products; in one case, a marquee software client's product run cost fell 45%. Management said outcome-based, revenue-share commercials with a backstop, and that the revenue upside is not in the deal financials.
Nagarro target: about 200 USD 1M+ customers with only 10 overlapping with Persistent's, per management's diligence view.

qa_highlights.question: Is high token cost pushing enterprise clients to IT services vendors, and is BFSI an early AI adopter?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said mid-market ISVs are the most AI-adopting segment, with BFSI and healthcare slower due to regulation. Clients are using small or open-weight models and token FinOps, with services firms brought in to optimise model choice and cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 90 bps large-deal amortisation hit persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai confirmed it will stay in the base for the next two to three quarters and gradually reduce as cost is optimised and revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD 650M large deal included in last quarter's TCV, and why are Q2 bookings softer?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said the deal was included in Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M, which included USD 125M ACV from it. Q2 ACV of USD 481M and TCV of USD 633.5M were described as a reasonable clip, with some slippage and no productivity-driven decline.

qa_highlights.question: Will software licence costs stay at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said it is a mix of licences embedded in deal products and Persistent's own tool investment; levels should be assessed on overall profitability as the reinvention practice grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin recovery expected post wage hike, and what is the year-end target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 16-17% aspirational margin range, not guidance, with optimisation and deal growth as the levers.

qa_highlights.question: What are quick wins from Nagarro after closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said a synergy plan can only be built after closing; a cooperation agreement already allows cross-selling. Nagarro has about 200 USD 1M+ customers with only 10 overlapping with Persistent's.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of acquisition debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai said 5-6% on a net basis, depending on timing; the Nagarro revolver is about 5 banks at SOFR-linked pricing and is being refinanced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the USD 50M one-time costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai said costs cover investment banking fees, bridge loan commitment fees, legal, regulatory filings, travel and funding costs; about USD 19-20M was incurred in Q2 and USD 25-30M is expected over the next 3-4 quarters.

risks_watch: Deal-win momentum: Q2 ACV and TCV were well below Q1 and management cited slippage and slower decisions linked to Middle East dynamics.
Europe revenue fell 8.5% YoY, and Healthcare and Lifesciences growth slowed to 12% YoY; management expects a recovery but did not commit to a timeline.
Margin pressure: 90 bps amortisation from the large deal and utilisation at 85.8% must reverse for the 16-17% aspiration to be reached.
Nagarro closing risk: Austria and Spain FDI and RBI approvals outstanding; USD 1.25B debt and equity raise and 5-6% debt cost are still to be executed.
Reported PAT and EPS will remain depressed by one-time costs over the next 3-4 quarters; ESOP vesting treatment still needs shareholder approval.

financial_highlights.change: +1.6% QoQ, +19.5% YoY; margin -100 bps QoQ, -130 bps YoY
Further USD 25-30M expected over next 2-4 quarters

key_quotes: We had a few deals that slipped over into this quarter, no excuses, we could have done better.
The slowdown of decision making in the last few weeks was pretty apparent.
So please review the data, it is included in the last quarter.
Please take this as an aspirational goal. We want to be in that bracket.
So, I would tend to say look at that TTM to TTM comparisons, rather than a comparison of a particular quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Nagarro closing path, the software reinvention thesis and the 16-17% margin aspiration, but explicitly cautious on near-term bookings, citing deal slippage and slower decisions linked to Middle East dynamics. Evasive on hard numbers: declined formal guidance, deflected the Q1-vs-Q2 TCV comparison to TTM growth, and would not comment on Nagarro's own debt.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management gave only an EBIT margin aspiration of 16-17% (explicitly not guidance) and said all segments should grow well. Q2 USD revenue grew 20% YoY, but TCV fell to USD 633.5M from USD 1,146.2M in Q1 as deals slipped amid Middle East-related slowdown, and utilisation dipped to 85.8% on hiring for the large-deal ramp, so backing is partial with no capacity additions
